record.original_question: For every classical solution f : [0, T] x R^3 -> [0, infinity) of the space-homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation with initial data f_0, is the pointwise bound f(t, v) <= sqrt(250 / (9 pi)) max_w f_0(w) valid for all (t, v) in [0, T] x R^3? If true, this would rule out finite-time blow-up through a universal L-infinity estimate.

evidence.quote: Conjecture 7.3. Let f : [0, T ]×R3 → [0, ∞) be a classical solution of (7.1), where Q is the Landau-Coulomb operator (7.2), and f (0, v) = f0 (v). Then, for all values of (t, v) ∈ [0, T ] × R3 , we have the inequality f (t, v) ≤ sqrt(250/(9π)) max f0 (v).
Conjecture 7.3, if true, rules out the finite time blow-up for solutions to (7.1) in the Landau-Coulomb case.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spatially homogeneous Landau equation with Coulomb potential on $\mathbb{R}^3$:
$$\partial_t f(t,v) = Q(f,f)(t,v), \qquad (t,v)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^3,$$
where the Landau collision operator with Coulomb interaction is
$$Q(f,f)(v) = \nabla_v\cdot\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^3} a(v-w)\bigl(f(w)\nabla f(v) - f(v)\nabla f(w)\bigr)\,dw\right),$$
with the matrix kernel
$$a(z) = \frac{1}{|z|}\left(I - \frac{z\otimes z}{|z|^2}\right), \qquad z\in\mathbb{R}^3\setminus\{0\}.$$
Let $f_0:\mathbb{R}^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a sufficiently smooth, rapidly decaying initial datum, and let $f:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a classical solution with $f(0,v)=f_0(v)$.

Prove or disprove: for every such classical solution,
$$f(t,v) \;\le\; \sqrt{\frac{250}{9\pi}}\;\sup_{w\in\mathbb{R}^3} f_0(w) \qquad\text{for all }(t,v)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^3.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Guillen and Silvestre (2023, "The Landau equation does not blow up", Acta Mathematica 2025) established global-in-time smoothness for the homogeneous Landau equation including the Coulomb case via monotonicity of the Fisher information, ruling out finite-time blow-up. However, this argument does not produce the explicit pointwise constant $\sqrt{250/(9\pi)}\,\|f_0\|_\infty$; the conjectured universal $L^\infty$ bound with that specific constant does not appear to be established in the literature, and recent work (e.g., the 2024 blow-down mechanism paper, and 2025 work on global $L^{3/2}$ solutions) does not prove this sharp bound. The conjecture therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: The Landau equation does not blow up
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions to the space-homogeneous Landau equation never blow up... includes the case of Landau equation with Coulomb interactions.
status_evidence.claim: Finite-time blow-up is ruled out for the homogeneous Landau-Coulomb equation, but via Fisher-information monotonicity rather than via the conjectured explicit pointwise constant.

status_evidence.title: A blow-down mechanism for the Landau-Coulomb equation
status_evidence.snippet: Explicit blow-down mechanism for a family of initial data... global well-posedness and exponential decay.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work studies dynamics of Landau-Coulomb solutions but does not establish the universal sharp $L^\infty$ bound with constant $\sqrt{250/(9\pi)}$.

status_evidence.title: Global Smooth Solutions to the Landau-Coulomb Equation in L^{3/2}
status_evidence.snippet: Global smooth solutions to the Landau-Coulomb equation in L^{3/2}.
status_evidence.claim: Recent regularity results for Landau-Coulomb do not give the conjectured explicit pointwise constant.
